lectures.note: For the final: Dr. Kaur said to really know peri-implant health, peri-implant mucositis and peri-implantitis for her part of the final, and her clinical questions will be based on them. In these notes that is the 2017 classification and the paragraphs after it. Practice telling the three apart on the S7 Patient Box cases in the Question Bank, and see Review for a step-by-step way to read an implant case.

lectures.label: S9

likelyTopics.t: Stage from CAL and bone loss, never from probing depth alone
Grading: start at B; the bone-loss/age ratio, smoking and HbA1c
Stage 4 complexity factors (the 2018 AAP/EFP tables)
Caries control is part of Phase I; the treatment sequence
Maintenance works: the Becker tooth-loss figures
Patient Box cases: stage and grade from the box
Recession types from the chart: RT1, RT2, RT3 and root coverage
Vertical incisions at the line angle, never through the papilla
A flap's base must be wider than its free edge
The sub-marginal incision
The suture chart: resorption, braided vs monofilament, tissue reaction
Suture techniques from a picture
Full vs partial thickness by procedure
McGuire & Nunn order: good, fair, poor, questionable, hopeless
McGuire & Nunn rates retention (maintainability); about 80% / 50% accurate
Diagnostic vs therapeutic: only McGuire & Nunn works diagnostically
Kwok & Caton (stability, whole dentition) and Miller & McEntire (molars)
Risk-stratified maintenance intervals
CAL = PD + recession, with its sign: negative recession in Salud
The host does 75% of the damage, bacteria 25%
Glickman furcation classes; Class II is the most regenerable
Debridement has one indication and is never combined with SRP
What SRP aims for, and re-evaluation at 4-6 weeks
Prophylaxis vs maintenance vs D4346
Fremitus is palpated; Miller mobility classes
Instrumentation: finger rests, scaling vs root planing, what the ultrasonic can't do
Attachment loss into the furcation drops the prognosis
Bower's furcation entrance depths from the CEJ
The maxillary buccal furcation is affected most
Primary cause is plaque-driven attachment loss; cervical enamel projections and their grades
One deep site in a stable mouth: look for a local cause
Furcation arrows, and the clinical exam before the radiograph
Osseous surgery: bone follows the gingiva, spare the furcation, debride the roots
Ineffective plaque control is the first contraindication; the 1981 root planing study
Furcation class from the Nabers probe, and the treatment by class
Best candidates: deep, narrow, 3-wall defects
Biologics: EMD (amelogenins), rhPDGF-BB, β-TCP
Regeneration vs repair; only histology proves it
Risk factors for a less predictable result
The AAP decision tree
Graft types and the GTR membrane
Her clinical cases: health, mucositis or peri-implantitis from the findings
Mucositis vs peri-implantitis: bone loss beyond remodeling is the difference
Health: no 3 mm cutoff; ~2 mm of first-year remodeling is physiologic; compare with the baseline
Treat it now: suppuration is active disease, mucositis is reversible; why peri-implantitis is hard to treat
Bleeding on probing, and radiographs: confirmatory, and the schedule
Smoking and implants: pathogens, immunity, nicotine, the studies
Risk assessment at every stage; treat periodontitis before implants
Success vs survival; Albrektsson's criteria
Ailing, failing, failed; a mobile implant comes out
Plaque biofilm, microbiology and the risk factor lists
Diabetes: control (HbA1c), not duration
IL-1 genotype, and with smoking
Never monotherapy: antibiotics alone are not indicated; when they are
Biofilms: only mechanical debridement removes them; barrier, β-lactamase, slow growth
Doses: his dosing chart and the drug slides
The host response does the damage: bacteria the key, the host the engine
The cascade: pellicle, complement, neutrophils then macrophages, IL-1
Bactericidal vs bacteriostatic; never combine one of each
Allergy, cephalosporin cross-reactivity and clindamycin
Interactions: warfarin, oral contraceptives, digoxin, alcohol
Local delivery: the stable maintenance site; PerioChip, Atridox, Arestin
Periostat: sub-antimicrobial doxycycline, collagenase, small added gains
NSAIDs, bisphosphonates and BRONJ; why to step lightly
Drug by drug: mechanism, ANUG, C. diff, tetracycline cautions, food
Augmentin, erythromycin, macrolides, pregnancy
Cairo RT1, RT2, RT3: how much root coverage to expect
Which graft: a covered graft is a CTG, under a coronally advanced flap
Inflammation causes recession; the factors only predispose
Keratinized gingiva: the 2 mm rule, and an FGG left exposed to create it
The acellular dermal matrix: what it is, when, and why it's covered
Untreated recession progresses; why treat it
Thin vs thick phenotype: the probe test and recession risk
Altered passive eruption: the types and their crown lengthening
Excessive gingival display: the cause from the findings, and its treatment
Pseudopockets and drug-induced enlargement
Esthetic norms: the lip, the gingival line, the golden proportion
The palate: its layers, the greater palatine bundle, the high vault

first-visit.title: Lower right, first visit
box: "My lower right gum bleeds when I floss"
28 teeth (third molars removed years ago for crowding). Bone loss like #30's at the mesial of #3 and #14; every other tooth probes 1-3 mm with the crest 1-2 mm from the CEJ
See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #28-#31

bleeding-gums.title: Bleeding gums at 23
box: "My gums bleed every time I brush, and they look puffy"

Bleeding on probing at 46% of sites; probing depths 3-5 mm throughout; at every site the CEJ is felt 3-5 mm below the gingival margin. Full-mouth radiographs: the crest sits 1-2 mm from the CEJ everywhere
See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #6-#11

long-teeth.title: Recession on the lower front teeth
box: "My lower front teeth look longer, and they hurt with cold"
Brushes hard, twice a day, with a medium brush
No bleeding on probing anywhere; probing depths 1-3 mm. Thin tissue with a narrow band of keratinized gingiva
The crest sits 1-2 mm from the CEJ everywhere except at #23, where the interproximal crest is about 3 mm lower
See the chart and the drawn view of #23-#26

furcation-19.title: A furcation on #19
box: Smokes 15 cigarettes a day, for 20 years
"Food packs around my lower left molar"
From the buccal the probe enters the furcation about 4 mm horizontally and stops against bone; from the lingual it does not enter
28 teeth, none lost to gum disease. Bone loss like this at #18, #19, #3, #14 and #30; the other teeth probe 1-3 mm with the crest 1-2 mm from the CEJ
See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #18-#21

triggers: Class II or III furcation involvement

deep-pocket-19.title: One deep pocket after Phase I
box: Full-mouth plaque score 12%; keeps every maintenance visit
Scaling and root planing of all quadrants 6 weeks ago for localized Stage 3 periodontitis (#3, #19 and #30); the other sites now probe 3 mm or less without bleeding
See the chart and the radiograph of #18-#21

figs.note: Compare the crest beside #19's mesial root with the crest at #20.

triggers: probing depth of 6 mm or more
vertical bone loss of 3 mm or more

implant-30.title: An implant at #30, three years on
box: Implant placed at #30 three years ago; the crown was seated 2.5 years ago. At the crown seating (the baseline): probing 3 mm all around, no bleeding, and the film showed the bone at the first thread, 1.5 mm below the platform
The crown is firm (no mobility). See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #29-#31

figs.title: #29-#31, today
figs.note: At the baseline film the bone met the implant at its first thread.

implant-19.title: An implant at #19, a year after its crown
box: #19 was lost to a root fracture. The implant was placed 16 months ago and its crown seated 12 months ago. At the crown seating (the baseline): probing 4-5 mm all around, no bleeding, and the film showed the bone 0.5 mm below the implant platform
Pink, firm mucosa; no bleeding or suppuration on gentle probing with a plastic probe; the crown is firm. See the chart, today's radiograph and the drawn view of #18-#20

figs.title: #18-#20, today
figs.note: At the baseline film the bone sat 0.5 mm below the platform.

implant-5.title: Bleeding around an implant at #5
box: "My gum bleeds around my implant when I brush"
Implant at #5 restored 4 years ago. At the crown seating (the baseline): probing 3 mm all around, no bleeding, and the bone 1.5 mm below the platform. His last annual film, 6 months ago, matched it

Red, swollen mucosa with plaque along the crown; profuse bleeding (a line) on gentle probing; no suppuration; the crown is firm. A periapical film was taken today. See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #4-#6

figs.title: #4-#6, today
figs.note: At the baseline film the bone sat 1.5 mm below the platform.

implant-14.title: An implant at #14, five years on
box: Quit smoking 2 years ago, after 30 years of a pack a day
Lost #14 and other teeth to periodontitis, which was treated before the implant went in. No maintenance visits in the last 3 years
At the crown seating 5 years ago (the baseline): probing 4 mm, no bleeding, and the bone 1 mm below the platform
The crown is firm (no mobility). See the chart, the radiograph and the drawn view of #13-#15

figs.title: #13-#15, today
figs.note: At the baseline film the bone sat 1 mm below the platform.

no-kg-24.title: A sensitive lower incisor with no keratinized gingiva
box: "This lower front tooth is sensitive, and it's hard to keep clean"
Brushes twice a day with a soft brush; plaque collects at the #24 margin
Treated for periodontitis; stable on periodontal maintenance since
Probing depths 1-3 mm; no bleeding on probing. The #24 facial margin sits in alveolar mucosa: no keratinized gingiva on that tooth, a good band on its neighbors
See the chart and the drawn view of #23-#26

recession-11.title: A long-looking canine
box: "My left canine looks long, and cold air makes it zing"
Probing depths 1-2 mm; no bleeding on probing. Facial recession on #10 and #11, with keratinized gingiva still apical to both
See the chart and the drawn view of #9-#12
